term: Affix grammar over a finite lattice
definition: Affix grammars over a finite lattice (AGFL) is a restricted type of affix grammar in which affixes can only assume finite sets of values.
details: It is aimed at natural language processing and other applications in linguistics. Some applications have been published. The AGFL project developed AGFL-based technology and made it available under the GNU GPL.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. At its heart it is a simple notion, once you strip away the fancy name. A small key that opens a much bigger door. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. That is Affix grammar over a finite lattice — a small key that opens a big door.
